Title: Calcium supplementation during pregnancy may reduce preterm delivery in high-risk populations
Author: Jose Villar and John T. Repke
Comment: The trial randomized 95 participants per arm and states that all subjects were analyzed in their originally assigned group; these randomized denominators are used for the requested ITT RR synthesis. Table V nevertheless labels the calcium pregnancy-outcome column N=94 (placebo N=95). The event counts corresponding to the supplied trial effect are 7/94 and 20/95 in Table V, while the synthesis denominator requested here is 95 randomized per arm; therefore the calcium row combines 7 observed events with the randomized denominator of 95. Title: Calcium supplementation for the prevention of pre-eclampsia
Author: Ashok Kumar et al.
Comment: The requested synthesis prefers randomized denominators, but the paper reports preterm-delivery events only among participants with delivery/neonatal outcome data (251 placebo and 273 calcium). Although 262 placebo and 290 calcium participants were randomized, assigning the reported events to those larger denominators would require an unsupported assumption. Therefore, the directly reported analyzed denominators were extracted. The paper reports an odds ratio, not a risk ratio; RR should be calculated downstream from the extracted arm-level counts.
